doc.title: Marshall Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 19, 2021

title: Discovering Sun Ra and joining in 1958
summary: Working at Revere Camera polishing lenses, Allen hears a Sun Ra record, learns the band rehearses six blocks away and joins in 1958.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well that attitude served you well trying to fit in with Sun Ra. Can you describe to me what it was that attracted you and compelled you to want to be part of that?

I was working at Revere Camera Company with polishing lenses, filters for cameras you know. I was a polisher, I was polishing. And I used to go to, around the corner to a record store and buy records because I liked to hear all kinds of records. I’m from the old school when all the bands was swinging. So the guy told me, “I’ve got a real nice record for you. It’s a thing with Sun Ra and Cecil Taylor and a whole lot of people is on it.” But I heard this band playing this tune “Super Blonde” and something else, and I said oh man, that’s a nice thing here. I was in that. And the guy says, “Hey man that’s Sun Ra. He rehearses every night and he’s always looking for talent.” I said, “Oh yeah?” He said, “Where you live?” I said, “I live on the south side.” He said, “Yeah, Sun Ra is on the south side, about
six blocks from where I live, rehearsing every night with the musicians.” I said, “Yeah, okay.” I took my horn when I got out of work that night to meet Sun Ra.
When you got to the house did you hear music coming out of it?
No it was Sun Ra used to have rehearsals, they had a lot of ballrooms in the old days you know, remember the ballrooms?

You’d put your tie on and dress up, and dance. So he would have an empty ballroom that he would rehearse in, you know, one they didn’t have no activity in. So that’s the way he built the band. So I went up there and I said well it’s in my neighborhood, about six blocks from where I lived. So I went up there with my horn and I’ve been there ever since. That was in 1958.
Yeah I did the math. I think that’s 63 years, Mr. Allen.
